claim: deploy.yml (Deploy to Production)'s workflow_run trigger acts only on this repository's own CI runs on main -- a push, or a manual (workflow_dispatch) run -- as far as a strict text reader can hold it (a direct, writer-only workflow_dispatch of deploy.yml itself runs the stages too, as before). ci-gate carries no job-level if (plain, quoted or spaced key) and one refusal step equal, line for line, to the allowed text: it reads the triggering run's event and head repository through env and exits 1 unless the event is 'push' or 'workflow_dispatch' and the repository is this one (a dispatch from a fork is refused); no line of ci-gate names GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_OUTPUT literally. The on: block, up to the next top-level key, equals the allowed one and no defaults: is set. The jobs: block holds only plain job keys (a quoted, flow-style, anchored or aliased job key, a job-level line that is not a plain lowercase key (quoted, tagged, anchored, explicit or merge key), a five-space indent, an unclosed quoted job-level value, a tab or a duplicate fails), the job set is fixed, and each job's single job-level if (block scalars read with their blank lines, plain scalars with their continuation lines) equals the one allowed: every workflow_run-startable job requires the own-run group (event push or workflow_dispatch, and this repository), rollback-guide is dispatch-only; no job is a reusable-workflow call; nothing sets continue-on-error. Key fix (founder, 2026-09-30, verbatim: "Approve all + widen (Recommended)"), as far as a strict text reader can hold it, reading the raw text (comment lines included, since a # line in a block scalar is content) with escaped line breaks joined, case-insensitively as GitHub reads contexts: no workflow-level key names secrets; nothing reads toJSON(secrets), secrets.* or secrets[...], and deploy.yml holds no backslash escape other than one before $, a backtick, a double quote or a line break, and no YAML anchor or alias, whatever its name's first character; ci-gate's job-level permissions is exactly {} and ci-gate has no uses: key in any step form (block, flow-style or quoted; so no cache save) and no secret; secrets.ADMIN_API_KEY is referenced exactly once, in the env of verify-orchestrator's step 'Verify 9/9 agents Active'. Held by scripts/check_deploy_own_pushes.py (gate-owned, run with python3 -I), whose --self-test plants exactly the 89 breaks it lists (52 for the own-run rule, 37 for the key fix), including a fork's dispatch, another event type and a missing repository check in a stage if and in the refusal step, and a missing repository check in deploy-audit's if; run by scripts/test_pr_audit_gate.py. Not held: how ci-gate's run: steps execute, and workflow-level keys other than on: and defaults: beyond the no-secret rule -- a job-level key on ci-gate other than if and permissions, another run: step in ci-gate, an env/path-file write other than the literal GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_OUTPUT, a workflow-level env (BASH_ENV, BASH_FUNC_*), permissions or run-name that names no secret, or a column-0 comment inside on: hiding an added trigger all pass the guard (known examples: `concurrency: |` before the refusal step; container, runs-on: self-hosted or services on ci-gate; job-level env: BASH_ENV; workflow-level BASH_FUNC_exit%%, which makes the refusal step exit 0 in local bash; a GITHUB_PATH or indirect env-file write; ci-gate run: steps that run what the triggering run controls (fetching head_sha and running a script, running a downloaded artifact of that run, or echoing head_commit.message into a shell; the action forms are refused by the key fix); the on: comment). Changes that only alter whether ci-gate goes green are still refused by every stage's and deploy-audit's if, pinned exactly and unchanged. The class (founder, 2026-09-30, verbatim picks "Describe the whole class, then fix the key (Recommended)" and then "Approve all + widen (Recommended)", which widened the round-5 ADR 0090 planner's sentence to his words): any ci-gate step or job-level value that runs, sources, or interpolates into any interpreter, image or environment anything the triggering run controls -- its checkout, its artifacts or caches, event fields the fork writes (head_commit.message, display_title), a github-script step's JavaScript, a container: or services: image. ci-gate has no if, so only gate ownership stops such a member from running; since the key fix it reaches, as far as rule 5's text reader can tell, no secret, no token scope and no action step (a job-level needs: or ${{ github.token }} still passes; neither carries a secret, and the token has no scope). (what is left open: tech-debt.d/2026-09-30-batch-open-prs-2026-09-29.md); ci-gate's first step (the conclusion check, pinned separately by ADR-0097's row) and GitHub's own YAML evaluation (a form this reader accepts but GitHub reads differently) (workflow_run runs main's copy, so the step first runs on the merge commit's Deploy run). Founder, 2026-09-30, on #534, verbatim picks: "Sign off, add deploy fix (Recommended)", "Yes, covered (Recommended)" (his sign-off covers the guard and this fragment, 33 gate-owned files), "Honest record (Recommended)" and "Describe the whole class, then fix the key (Recommended)" (this record names what the guard does not hold; he re-confirmed the sign-off on the files it changes) and "Also allow manual runs" (so pr_audit_gate.py's CI-side merge re-entry, a workflow_dispatch of CI on main, still reaches the deploy audit). "Approve all + widen (Recommended)" approved the key fix's three changes; #534's record had dated all three to the earlier answer, which approved scoping the key only (corrected in ADR 0097's key-fix section).
